sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: This visa stream is for citizens of the People's Republic of China, Brunei, Cambodia, Philippines, Laos, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam or Timor Leste who travel often to Australia for tourism or business visitor activities.

sections.heading: Overview > Requirements
sections.text:
You must hold a passport from and be a citizen of one of the following countries:

- The People’s Republic of China
- Brunei
- Cambodia
- Philippines
- Laos
- Indonesia
- Malaysia
- Singapore
- Thailand
- Vietnam
- Timor Leste

You must also provide biometrics at an Australian Biometric Collection Centre (ABCC). For more information, visit Biometrics.

For information on ABCCs including updates, appointment bookings and opening times for each location, visit Our Offices outside Australia.

We will notify you by email on how to provide your biometrics. It is important that you arrange to have your biometrics captured as soon as possible to avoid any delays in processing your visa. For visas that may not require biometrics, you can explore your visa options.

sections.heading: Overview > With this visa you can
sections.text:
- be a tourist, cruise or have a holiday
- visit family or friends
- undertake business visitor activities

sections.heading: Overview > How long you can stay
sections.text: The visa can be granted for up to 10 years. Stay up to 3 months each time you enter.

sections.heading: Overview > Processing time
sections.text: Processing times for this visa are unavailable.

sections.heading: About this visa > With this visa you can
sections.text:
- visit family or friends
- be here as a tourist, for a cruise or a holiday
- undertake business visitor activities

sections.heading: About this visa > How long you can stay
sections.text:
The visa can be granted for up to 10 years. You can enter Australia as often as you like while the visa is valid but you can only stay:

- up to 3 months each time you enter
- for 12 months in total in any 24-month period

Your visa grant letter will tell you how long you can stay.

sections.heading: About this visa > Stay longer
sections.text:
You can't stay in Australia longer by extending this visa. You must apply for another visa.

You can apply for a new visa if your visa does not have a condition that prevents further stay, such as condition 8503. You might be able to request a waiver of the no further stay condition in limited circumstances.

You must not breach condition 8573, no more than 12 months stay in any 24-month period, or condition 8531, must not remain in Australia beyond visa period, if they are attached to your visa.

You can explore your visa options.

sections.heading: About this visa > Include family
sections.text:
You can't include family members in your application. A separate application must be made for each member of your family, including those listed on your passport.

Newborn child

Find out what to do if your child is born after you apply.

sections.heading: About this visa > Cost
sections.text:
The visa costs for each applicant (concessions apply in limited circumstances).

You might also have to pay other costs for health checks, police certificates and biometrics.

Use the Visa Pricing Estimator to work out what your visa will cost. The estimator does not take into account the other costs.

Cost concession for eligible Timor-Leste Visitor visa applicants

From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Timor-Leste citizens who lodge a valid visa application.

We will charge eligible applicants the lower visa application cost during the application process in ImmiAccount. We will recognise eligible applicants by the valid passport from the specified countries used in the application when they apply.

The applicant must hold a valid passport issued by Timor-Leste.

sections.heading: About this visa > Apply from
sections.text: To be eligible for this visa, you must be outside Australia when you apply and when we decide your application.

sections.heading: About this visa > Your obligations
sections.text: You must meet all visa conditions and obey Australian laws.

sections.heading: About this visa > Health insurance
sections.text:
We recommend you take out health insurance to cover any unforeseen medical treatment you might need in Australia. You are personally liable for all your healthcare costs while you are in Australia. Insurance can help limit your financial liability.

See what we consider adequate health insurance.

Learn more about health insurance for overseas visitors.

Reciprocal healthcare agreements

Some countries have a reciprocal healthcare agreement with Australia. Find out more from Services Australia about reciprocal healthcare agreements.

sections.heading: About this visa > Travel
sections.text:
You can travel outside Australia and return as many times as you want while the visa is valid.

The time you spend outside Australia does not extend the visa.

sections.heading: About this visa > Visa label
sections.text: We will digitally link your visa to your passport. You will not get a label in your passport.

sections.heading: Eligibility
sections.text: You must meet all of these criteria to be eligible for the Visitor visa Frequent traveller stream.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet our character requirement
sections.text: You must meet our character requirement.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have paid back your debt to the Australian Government
sections.text: If you or any family members (including those who don't apply for the visa with you) owe the Australian government money, you or they must have paid it back or arranged to pay it back.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have enough money
sections.text:
You must have enough money to:

- support yourself while you are in Australia
- leave Australia at the end of your stay

sections.heading: Eligibility > Be a genuine visitor
sections.text:
You must only intend to:

- stay temporarily in Australia
- obey any condition and stay period attached to your visa

sections.heading: Eligibility > Best interests of the child
sections.text: We might not grant this visa if it is not in the best interests of an applicant under 18.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Check your passport
sections.text: You need a valid passport or other travel document for this visa. If you plan to get a new passport, do this before you apply.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Organise health examinations
sections.text:
You can complete your health examinations before you apply or you can wait until we tell you to have them.

Find out more about our Health Requirements.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Get help with your application
sections.text:
You don’t have to use a migration agent to apply for any visa. But if you want to, see how to find a registered migration agent.

Anyone can help you fill out forms or give you general help with your application. But you must let us know if you want someone to:

- receive your correspondence
- provide immigration assistance and act for you

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Provide accurate information
sections.text:
Provide accurate information.

See what happens if you can't prove your identity or don't provide true information.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Identity documents
sections.text:
You must prove your identity to us. If you can't prove your identity:

- we will refuse your visa application
- we might not grant you another visa for 10 years
- we might not grant any family members you listed on your application a visa for 10 years

Provide the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details and passport issue and expiry dates.

Also provide:

- a national identity card, if you have one
- proof of change of name, if applicable, such as:

- a marriage or divorce certificate
- change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority
- documents that show other names you have been known by

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Genuine visitor documents
sections.text:
Provide as much proof as you can to show you are visiting Australia as a temporary, genuine visitor:

- proof you have enough money for your stay and to leave Australia, such as personal bank statements, pay slips, audited accounts, tax records or credit card limit.
- evidence of financial dependency to someone travelling with you if you are aged 18 or older
- a letter from your relative or friend in Australia, inviting you to visit. The relative or friend must be an Australian citizen or permanent resident. The letter needs to state:

- their relationship to you
- the purpose of your visit and length of stay
- if you will be staying with them

If this person will be paying for your stay, provide proof of their funds.
- your plans while in Australia

Proof that you have reasons to return home:

- a letter from your employer stating you plan to return to your job
- proof that you study at a school, college or university back home
- proof that you have immediate family members back home
- proof that you can return home
- proof that you own a house or other major assets back home

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Business visitor documents
sections.text:
Tell us what business visitor activities you plan to do in Australia. You could provide:

- an invitation from a host organisation
- conference registration details
- a letter from your employer stating why you are visiting
- your plans for your stay and details of your Australian business contacts
- proof of your current employment and professional qualifications
- evidence your company is an active business, such as an annual report
- evidence of prior contact with Australian businesses

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Character documents
sections.text:
Provide any military service record or discharge papers if this applies.

We may ask you to provide a police certificate. To learn more visit Character requirements.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Tell us you are getting help documents
sections.text:
To nominate someone to:

- receive your correspondence, use Form 956a Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration advice, use Form 956 Advice by a migration agent/exempt person of providing immigration assistance
- act for you but not provide immigration assistance, let us know in writing what they can do on your behalf (such as submit or withdraw an application for you). Upload your written notification in ImmiAccount

See more about getting help with your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Additional documents for applicants under 18
sections.text:
If anyone with a legal right to decide where an applicant under 18 lives is not visiting Australia, they must complete either:

- Form 1229 - Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years
- a statutory declaration giving their consent for the child to visit Australia on this visa

Include a document with the signature and photo of the person who completed the form or declaration, such as a:

- passport
- driver’s licence

Also provide a birth certificate showing the names of both parents. If you can’t provide a birth certificate, provide one of the following:

- identification pages of a family book showing the names of both parents
- identification pages of an identification document issued by the government
- identification pages of a court-issued document that proves your identity
- identification pages of a family census register

Provide:

- adoption papers or parental court orders, if applicable
- proof of enrolment at school, college or university

If the applicant is not staying with a relative or legal guardian, provide Form 1257 - Undertaking declaration. The person they are staying with must sign the form

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Additional documents for dependent applicants 18 or older
sections.text:
If you are a dependant aged 18 or older, also provide:

- proof of your relationship with the person you depend on such as a birth or marriage certificate
- proof that you have been financially dependent on this person for at least 12 months immediately before you apply, such as:

- proof that you live with them
- proof of your current studies or tax records

- adoption papers or parental court orders, if applicable

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > For online applications > Translate
sections.text:
Have all non-English documents translated into English.

Provide original and translated documents in your application.

Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters.

Translators outside Australia don't have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their:

- full name
- address and telephone number
- qualifications and experience in the language they are translating

These details must be in English.

Note: You don't need to have any documents certified.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > For online applications > Scan or photograph
sections.text:
Scan or photograph all documents (English and non-English) in colour.

The scans and photos must be clear and legible.

If a document is more than one page, save it all as one file.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather your documents > Prepare your documents > For online applications > Attach
sections.text:
Attach a document only once, even if you are using it to show more than one thing.

Learn more about attaching documents.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > Apply online
sections.text:
- Log in or create an ImmiAccount.
- Attach documents.
- Have family applications processed together.
- Pay the application fee. We will not process your application until you pay the fee.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply
sections.text:
We will let you know when we have received your application and documents.

There are other things you need to know and might need to do.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Travel
sections.text: Don't make arrangements to travel to Australia until we let you know, in writing, that you have been granted a visa.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Biometrics
sections.text: We will let you know if you need to provide biometrics.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Information about biometric collection for Frequent Traveller stream applicants residing in China
sections.text:
Biometric collection in the People’s Republic of China is currently available only in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. Applicants who need to complete biometrics must arrange an appointment to attend an Australian Biometrics Collection Centre (ABCC). This includes attending ABCC’s located in other countries. For a complete list of biometric collection locations, visit biometrics.

For information on ABCCs including updates, appointment bookings and opening times for each location, visit Our Offices outside Australia.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Health exams
sections.text: We will let you know if you need health examinations.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Send more information
sections.text:
If you did not send us all documents when you applied, do so as soon as you can, via ImmiAccount.

We might also ask you to provide more information.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Mistakes on your application
sections.text:
Let us know as soon as you can if you made a mistake on your application.

Complete Form 1023 Notification of incorrect answers .

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Change who you nominate to help with your application
sections.text:
Let us know if you no longer want someone to:

- receive your correspondence - complete Form 956a Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration advice - complete Form 956 Advice by a migration agent/exempt person of providing immigration assistance
- act for you - let us know in writing by uploading your advice in ImmiAccount

See more about withdrawing your nomination.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
Tell us if things change after you lodge your application but before we have made a decision.

Things you need to let us know about include:

- you want to withdraw your application
- changes to your phone number, address or passport
- changes to your relationship status
- the birth of a child

sections.heading: Step by step > Visa outcome
sections.text:
We will let you know our decision on your visa application in writing. We will tell you:

- your visa grant number
- the date your visa starts
- your visa conditions

Keep a copy of our decision with you when in Australia.

If we refuse your visa, we will let you know in writing. We will tell you why we refused and whether you have a right to a review of the decision.

Step Summary

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Coming to Australia
sections.text:
Before you travel

Check your travel documents

You must have:

- a valid visa to enter Australia
- a valid passport or other travel document

At the border

Complete an Incoming Passenger Card

Everyone who arrives in Australia must complete an Incoming Passenger Card.

Using the SmartGate

A SmartGate is an automated process that uses facial recognition technology and your ePassport. You might be able to leave the airport faster if you use SmartGates.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > In Australia
sections.text:
What you must do on your visa

You must meet all visa conditions and obey Australian laws. See your conditions in VEVO or your visa grant letter.

Learn more about visa conditions and how they work.

Tell us about a change in your situation

Things you need to let us know about include:

- changes to your phone number, email, address or passport
- changes to your relationship status
- the birth of a child

See how to let us know if there is a change in your situation.

What you can do on your visa

This visa lets you:

- cruise or have a holiday
- visit family or friends
- undertake business visitor activities
- study for up to 3 months

Volunteer work tourism schemes

You can't work in Australia on a Visitor visa, but you might be able to do volunteer work.

Travel on your visa

You can travel to and from Australia as many times as you want while the visa is valid

See how long you can stay

See when you must leave in VEVO.

Stay longer

You can't stay in Australia longer by extending this visa. You must apply for a new visa if you want to stay longer. See your options.

Prove you have a visa

To prove you have a visa and show your conditions to someone, use VEVO.

Request your international movement records to get proof of your travel in and out of Australia.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Leaving Australia
sections.text:
Before you leave

Check your travel documents

You must have a valid passport or other travel document to leave Australia.

Ensure your visa is still valid

See what to do if your visa has expired or is about to expire.

At the border

Departures SmartGate

We have an automated process that uses facial recognition technology and your ePassport. You might be able to leave the airport faster if you use SmartGates.

After you leave

International Movement Record

Request your international movement records to get proof of your travel in and out of Australia.
